hook.line: How to write a marketing strategy in four simple steps, so you see where you went wrong.
hook.visual: Wide shot of her in a chair with a laptop, a black 'How to write a Marketing Strategy' title on top, word captions mid-frame; she raises an open hand.

beats.what: Title card plus promise of four steps and where you went wrong
Cut: she turns the laptop toward camera
Close-up of the laptop: 1/4 Audience strategy slide with the questions to answer
Slide 2/4 Brand strategy: who are you, why should anyone care
Third step, content persona, back on her face
Zoom punch on 'online personality, a lifestyle'
Slides 2-4 side by side; finally, customer journey and funnel
Slide 4/4 Marketing funnels: where, when, what you post
Back on her: marketing without this is driving without a roadmap
Close: when clients answer these, their brands blow up

why_it_works: Numbered 1/4-4/4 slides show progress, so viewers know how much is left
Laptop slides filmed in hand feel like a peek at real client work, not a deck
'100% of you don't know your audience' gives a sharp sting early in step one
The roadmap analogy near the end makes the cost of skipping the steps concrete
weaknesses: Slides filmed at an angle are partly cut off and hard to read on a phone
No CTA despite the 4.3k shares; a save prompt would fit a checklist
Last 15 s are generic motivation after the useful content ends
for_robert: Use a numbered progress marker (1/4, 2/4) on screen; Fred could hold up each step number like a card.
